main_issue: Whether alcohol for the housewarming can be kept in the flat; resolved by keeping it in a cooler box outside the front door.

A-B.evidence: B said 'looks good to me' (T2) and later 'that works for me' (T19). A said 'a cooler outside works for me' (T17) and 'that's settled' (T21). They never addressed each other directly.

A-C.evidence: C proposed the cooler outside the door (T13) and asked A (T15). A replied 'a cooler outside works for me' (T17).

A-D.evidence: A asked D to clarify (T3, T8). D objected to alcohol (T4, T9), then agreed to the cooler outside (T14). A said 'that's settled' (T21).

B-C.evidence: C asked B whether the cooler works for his manager (T18). B said 'that works for me... Thanks for sorting it out' (T19).

B-D.evidence: B needs drinks for his manager (T10), against D's no-alcohol-at-home position (T9). Both ended up accepting the cooler outside (T14, T19). They did not address each other directly.

C-D.evidence: D turned down C's kitchen idea (T12), then accepted the cooler outside: 'I can agree to that. Thanks, Agent C.' (T14).
